phases.description: Carry the exact problem brief into a unified administration, identity, and fleet-management boundary.

steps.title: Freeze the exact live problem brief
steps.content:
Title: Design a Secure Multi-Cloud Kubernetes Architecture
Description: Design a multi-cloud Kubernetes platform that manages workloads across multiple cloud providers with consistent policies, service mesh, and centralized configuration.
Requirements:
1. Manage Kubernetes across clouds
2. Implement consistent policies
3. Deploy applications anywhere
4. Monitor multi-cloud resources
5. Implement service mesh
6. Ensure security compliance
7. Synchronize configurations
8. Handle hybrid connectivity
Constraints:
1. Unified management interface
2. Support AWS, Azure, and on-prem
3. Network latency under 100ms
4. Implement zero-trust networking
5. Maintain policy consistency
Hints:
1. Anthos for multi-cloud management
2. GKE for Google Cloud clusters
3. Anthos Service Mesh for networking
4. Config Sync for GitOps
5. Anthos Config Management for policies
6. Cloud Monitoring for observability

steps.title: Add the unified management interface
steps.content: Represent the single operator-facing interface for viewing fleet membership, configuration status, policy results, and resource health. The brief does not specify a product or implementation for this interface.

component.label: Multi-Cloud Kubernetes Admin Console
component.description: Unified operator interface for the registered Kubernetes fleet.

properties.purpose: Present one operator-facing view of registered clusters, configuration reconciliation, policy findings, and resource health; leave the console implementation open.

component.highlightReason: A unified management interface is an explicit constraint in the frozen brief.

steps.title: Represent the identity boundary
steps.content: Treat this as a provider-neutral trust boundary, not a claim that one identity integration works across the fleet. Define operator federation separately from workload identity; configure provider-specific issuer trust, subject/audience mapping, and least-privilege RBAC for each cluster. The brief does not choose an identity provider or federation model. The OAuth and MFA flags are proposed settings, not evidence that federation, authorization, or compliance is deployed and verified.

component.label: Operator and Workload Identity
component.description: Authentication boundary for operators and authorized platform workloads.

properties.purpose: Represent operator and workload authentication with scoped identities and explicit authorization; configure and verify provider-specific federation, trust mappings, and least-privilege cluster RBAC rather than assuming a shared identity integration.

component.highlightReason: The zero-trust constraint requires identity to be explicit at access boundaries.

steps.title: Authenticate console access
steps.content: Require the console to validate authenticated, scoped operator identity before exposing fleet controls or sensitive cluster status. Establish and test the console's trust and role mapping for the selected identity provider; an identity-flow edge alone does not prove federation or authorization coverage.

connection.label: Authenticated operator access
connection.description: The console must validate scoped claims and configured roles; the edge represents the intended boundary, not proof of federated login or complete audit coverage.

steps.title: Add the hinted fleet-management role
steps.content: Use the existing generic custom component for Anthos because the catalog has no dedicated Anthos fleet-management type. Treat supported cluster registration and control-plane reachability as items to verify for each target environment.

component.label: Anthos Fleet Management
component.description: Candidate multi-cloud Kubernetes fleet-management control plane.

properties.subtitle: Fleet registration and centralized control
properties.purpose: Represent the Anthos fleet-management role named in the problem hint; validate cluster support, registration, permissions, and reachability for each target environment before implementation.
properties.notes: Candidate control plane from the problem hint; provider and on-prem support must be verified for the selected cluster environments.

component.highlightReason: Anthos is named in the brief hint, while the component catalog has no dedicated Anthos entry.

steps.title: Route fleet administration through the control plane
steps.content: Send operator fleet actions from the unified console through the fleet-management boundary. Keep cluster-specific runtime ownership at each environment.

connection.label: Fleet administration
connection.description: Authorized console actions reach the fleet control plane for registered-cluster operations.

steps.title: Authorize fleet-control requests
steps.content: Authorize fleet-control operations with a verified caller identity and explicit roles. Bind the control plane's identity to each provider or cluster using supported federation and narrowly scoped permissions; validate denied as well as allowed actions.

connection.label: Scoped fleet identity
connection.description: Fleet operations are intended to validate callers and roles after provider-specific trust and permission bindings are configured and tested.

steps.title: Represent Google Cloud Kubernetes
steps.content: Use the catalog Kubernetes component with its supported GKE distribution value. The brief does not provide cluster count, version, node count, or workload capacity, so leave those values unspecified.

component.label: Google Cloud GKE Cluster
component.description: Google Cloud Kubernetes runtime represented by the GKE hint.

properties.purpose: Run Kubernetes workloads in Google Cloud and expose the cluster to the fleet control, configuration, policy, mesh, and monitoring flows.

component.highlightReason: GKE is explicitly named as the Google Cloud cluster option in the frozen hints.

steps.title: Represent the AWS Kubernetes environment
steps.content: Represent an AWS Kubernetes runtime using the existing catalog Kubernetes type. The brief does not name an AWS distribution, so leave its distribution and sizing unspecified for the platform owner to select.

component.label: AWS Kubernetes Environment
component.description: AWS Kubernetes runtime; distribution and sizing remain to be selected.

properties.purpose: Represent the AWS Kubernetes runtime that must be supported; select its distribution and operational ownership with the platform team.

component.highlightReason: AWS support is an explicit constraint, but the brief does not choose a Kubernetes distribution.

steps.title: Represent the Azure Kubernetes environment
steps.content: Represent an Azure Kubernetes runtime using the existing catalog Kubernetes type. The brief does not name an Azure distribution, so leave its distribution and sizing unspecified for the platform owner to select.

component.label: Azure Kubernetes Environment
component.description: Azure Kubernetes runtime; distribution and sizing remain to be selected.

properties.purpose: Represent the Azure Kubernetes runtime that must be supported; select its distribution and operational ownership with the platform team.

component.highlightReason: Azure support is an explicit constraint, but the brief does not choose a Kubernetes distribution.

steps.title: Represent the on-premises Kubernetes environment
steps.content: Use the catalog Kubernetes type without setting a distribution, version, or sizing. The brief requires on-prem support but does not specify the environment, so confirm its cluster implementation and connectivity before rollout.

component.label: On-Prem Kubernetes Environment
component.description: On-premises Kubernetes runtime; distribution and connectivity details remain open.

properties.purpose: Represent the required on-premises Kubernetes runtime while leaving distribution, ownership, network topology, and sizing to the environment owner.

component.highlightReason: On-premises Kubernetes support is explicit, while no distribution or topology is specified.

steps.title: Register the GKE environment with the fleet
steps.content: Connect the GKE runtime to fleet management using the registration mechanism supported by the selected Anthos setup. Confirm permissions and reachability before treating registration as complete.

connection.label: GKE fleet registration
connection.description: Candidate GKE registration path; verify the selected fleet integration, identity binding, permissions, and reachability before relying on management operations.

steps.title: Register the AWS environment with the fleet
steps.content: Represent the AWS registration path, then validate that the selected AWS cluster and Anthos setup support the required fleet operations.

connection.label: AWS fleet registration
connection.description: Candidate AWS registration path; verify distribution support, provider-specific identity binding, scoped permissions, and reachability before relying on management operations.

steps.title: Register the Azure environment with the fleet
steps.content: Represent the Azure registration path, then validate that the selected Azure cluster and Anthos setup support the required fleet operations.

connection.label: Azure fleet registration
connection.description: Candidate Azure registration path; verify distribution support, provider-specific identity binding, scoped permissions, and reachability before relying on management operations.

steps.title: Register the on-prem environment with the fleet
steps.content: Represent the on-prem registration path and leave network prerequisites, identity, and supported operations for the on-prem and platform owners to validate.

connection.label: On-prem fleet registration
connection.description: Candidate on-prem registration path; verify the selected integration, identity binding, scoped permissions, and owner-approved network reachability before relying on management operations.

steps.title: Confirm the fleet membership boundary
steps.content: Use Anthos as the hinted candidate fleet control plane, subject to verifying support and operational access for every chosen GKE, AWS, Azure, and on-prem environment. Do not infer a cluster count or distribution from this diagram.

decision.question: How should the fleet-management boundary be established?
decision.chosen: Treat Anthos as the candidate unified control plane and verify supported registration, permissions, and reachability for each target environment.
decision.chosenReason: Anthos is the multi-cloud hint in the brief, while the exact cluster distributions and support matrix are not specified.

alternatives.option: Assume every Kubernetes environment is automatically supported
alternatives.tradeoff: The fleet may lack required registration or management capabilities for a selected environment.

alternatives.option: Choose a separate control plane for each cloud
alternatives.tradeoff: Operators may lose the unified management interface required by the brief.

properties.notes: Candidate scope: register supported GKE, AWS, Azure, and on-prem Kubernetes environments in Anthos Fleet; verify support and reachability before rollout.

steps.title: Represent the configuration source
steps.content: The Config Sync hint implies a GitOps source. Use the generic custom component because the catalog has no provider-neutral Git repository node; leave the Git provider, repository layout, and approval workflow open.

component.label: GitOps Configuration Source
component.description: Version-controlled desired configuration consumed by Config Sync.

properties.subtitle: Git provider to be selected
properties.purpose: Store reviewed desired Kubernetes configuration for Config Sync; choose repository ownership, branch protections, approvals, and layout with the platform team.
properties.notes: No Git provider or repository workflow is specified in the problem brief.

component.highlightReason: Config Sync is named as the GitOps hint, but no repository product is specified or represented in the catalog.

steps.title: Add the hinted configuration synchronizer
steps.content: Use the existing Configuration Management component with Google Config Sync selected. Keep reconciliation status and drift visible to operators.

component.label: Config Sync Reconciliation
component.description: GitOps reconciliation of approved desired Kubernetes configuration.

properties.purpose: Reconcile reviewed configuration from the selected Git source with supported fleet clusters and report synchronization state and drift.

component.highlightReason: The existing configuration-management component now exposes Google Config Sync as a selectable tool.

steps.title: Deliver reviewed desired state to Config Sync
steps.content: Let Config Sync read the approved repository state. Define credential scope and change approval with the repository owner rather than assuming them here.

connection.label: Reviewed desired configuration
connection.description: Config Sync consumes version-controlled desired state from the selected Git provider.

steps.title: Reconcile configuration on GKE
steps.content: If the repository contains application manifests, treat Config Sync as a candidate way to apply those Kubernetes resources on GKE after validating APIs, images, secrets, and dependencies. A successful reconciliation only reports desired-state sync; it does not prove the application is portable, healthy, or available.

connection.label: GKE desired state
connection.description: Candidate reconciliation of reviewed Kubernetes resources on GKE; verify integration and workload readiness separately.

steps.title: Reconcile configuration on AWS
steps.content: If the repository contains application manifests, use this as a candidate deployment path only after confirming the selected AWS distribution and Config Sync integration support the required APIs. Validate images, secrets, dependencies, and workload health independently; reconciliation is not proof that the application is portable or available.

connection.label: AWS desired state
connection.description: Candidate reconciliation on the selected AWS cluster after integration support is verified; validate workload readiness separately.

steps.title: Reconcile configuration on Azure
steps.content: If the repository contains application manifests, use this as a candidate deployment path only after confirming the selected Azure distribution and Config Sync integration support the required APIs. Validate images, secrets, dependencies, and workload health independently; reconciliation is not proof that the application is portable or available.

connection.label: Azure desired state
connection.description: Candidate reconciliation on the selected Azure cluster after integration support is verified; validate workload readiness separately.

steps.title: Reconcile configuration on-prem
steps.content: If the repository contains application manifests, use this as a candidate deployment path only after validating on-prem distribution support, identity, and reachability. Check API compatibility, images, secrets, dependencies, and workload health separately; reconciliation does not prove portability or availability.

connection.label: On-prem desired state
connection.description: Candidate reconciliation on the selected on-prem cluster over an owner-approved path; verify integration and workload readiness separately.

steps.title: Add the hinted policy-management role
steps.content: Represent Anthos Config Management policy responsibilities separately from desired-state synchronization, using the existing Configuration Management component with the matching tool selected.

component.label: Anthos Config Management Policies
component.description: Policy evaluation and compliance controls across registered clusters.

properties.purpose: Evaluate and report an owner-defined Kubernetes policy baseline across supported fleet members. Define provider-specific rule coverage, enforcement, exceptions, and evidence; the component does not itself establish regulatory compliance.

component.highlightReason: The catalog component reuses existing editable configuration-management properties for Anthos policy.

steps.title: Evaluate policy on GKE
steps.content: Evaluate the owner-approved policy baseline on GKE and report rule results and gaps to the operator. Treat this as evidence for configured controls only; compliance depends on an agreed standard and verified coverage.

connection.label: GKE policy evaluation
connection.description: Configured policy results for GKE are reported; the result is not a compliance certification.

steps.title: Evaluate policy on AWS
steps.content: Evaluate the approved policy intent against the selected AWS environment, making unsupported rules and exceptions visible. Confirm equivalent rule semantics and evidence for this distribution; do not infer compliance from a successful evaluation.

connection.label: AWS policy evaluation
connection.description: Supported AWS rule results and gaps are reported; interpretation and compliance evidence require an approved baseline.

steps.title: Evaluate policy on Azure
steps.content: Evaluate the approved policy intent against the selected Azure environment, making unsupported rules and exceptions visible. Confirm equivalent rule semantics and evidence for this distribution; do not infer compliance from a successful evaluation.

connection.label: Azure policy evaluation
connection.description: Supported Azure rule results and gaps are reported; interpretation and compliance evidence require an approved baseline.

steps.title: Evaluate policy on-prem
steps.content: Evaluate the approved policy intent against on-prem resources while retaining explicit local exceptions and evidence. Confirm equivalent rule semantics and evidence for this distribution; do not infer compliance from a successful evaluation.

connection.label: On-prem policy evaluation
connection.description: Supported on-prem rule results and gaps are reported; interpretation and compliance evidence require an approved baseline.

steps.title: Separate configuration reconciliation from policy enforcement
steps.content: Keep desired-state synchronization and compliance policy as related but separately observable responsibilities. Confirm supported behavior and policy exceptions with the platform owners.

decision.question: How should configuration and policy responsibilities be divided?
decision.chosen: Use Config Sync to reconcile version-controlled desired state and Anthos Config Management to evaluate and report policy separately.
decision.chosenReason: The brief names both Config Sync and Anthos Config Management, and separate status makes drift distinguishable from policy violations.

alternatives.option: Treat successful synchronization as proof of policy compliance
alternatives.tradeoff: A configuration can reconcile successfully while still violating an approved policy.

alternatives.option: Combine policy rules into an undocumented synchronization step
alternatives.tradeoff: Operators may not be able to distinguish configuration drift from compliance findings.

properties.purpose: Reconcile version-controlled desired state and report drift separately from Anthos Config Management policy evaluation and compliance findings.

steps.title: Add the hinted service-mesh role
steps.content: Use the existing Service Mesh component with Anthos Service Mesh selected as a candidate. The `mtls` property records desired configuration, not deployed enforcement. Verify supported cluster versions, workload coverage, trust-domain and certificate-authority interoperability, and cross-cluster routing before relying on mesh identity or policy.

component.label: Anthos Service Mesh
component.description: Service-mesh role for workload communication and zero-trust controls.

properties.purpose: Represent the intended authenticated workload communication, traffic policy, and mesh observability where supported; configure interoperable workload identity and trust domains, then verify per-workload mTLS enforcement and feature coverage.

component.highlightReason: The existing Service Mesh component now offers the exact Anthos provider and retains its mTLS and traffic-policy properties.

steps.content: Represent service-mesh integration with GKE and verify the selected mesh capabilities and workload identity configuration.

connection.label: GKE workload traffic and identity
connection.description: Intended GKE mesh integration; verify identity trust, policy coverage, and mTLS enforcement on selected workloads.

steps.title: Attach the mesh to AWS workloads
steps.content: Represent service-mesh integration with the selected AWS cluster and validate cross-environment feature support before relying on mesh policy.

connection.label: AWS workload traffic and identity
connection.description: Intended AWS mesh integration; verify distribution support, cross-cloud identity trust, policy coverage, and mTLS enforcement on selected workloads.

steps.title: Attach the mesh to Azure workloads
steps.content: Represent service-mesh integration with the selected Azure cluster and validate cross-environment feature support before relying on mesh policy.

connection.label: Azure workload traffic and identity
connection.description: Intended Azure mesh integration; verify distribution support, cross-cloud identity trust, policy coverage, and mTLS enforcement on selected workloads.

steps.title: Attach the mesh to on-prem workloads
steps.content: Represent service-mesh integration with the on-prem cluster and verify its connectivity, identity, and feature compatibility.

connection.label: On-prem workload traffic and identity
connection.description: Intended on-prem mesh integration; verify runtime support, identity trust, network reachability, policy coverage, and mTLS enforcement on selected workloads.

steps.title: Represent the hybrid connectivity boundary
steps.content: Use the generic custom component because the catalog has no provider-neutral hybrid connectivity node and the brief chooses no network product or topology. Define routing, address space, DNS, firewall/egress rules, MTU, ownership, and path measurement for each required route. A service mesh does not create underlying network reachability.

component.label: Hybrid Connectivity Boundary
component.description: Owner-defined network paths between on-prem and cloud environments.

properties.subtitle: Network implementation to be selected
properties.purpose: Represent intended owner-approved paths between on-premises and cloud Kubernetes environments; validate topology, routing, non-overlapping address space, DNS, firewall/egress, MTU, security controls, and operational ownership for each path.
properties.notes: The problem specifies a network-latency target but no topology, regions, traffic profile, or network product.

component.highlightReason: Hybrid connectivity is required, but the component catalog has no generic hybrid path and the brief selects no network technology.

steps.title: Connect the on-prem environment to the hybrid boundary
steps.content: Show the on-prem environment's owner-approved path into the hybrid connectivity boundary. The exact network design remains undecided.

connection.label: On-prem network path
connection.description: Intended on-prem route; validate routing, DNS, firewall/egress, address compatibility, and reachability independently of mesh policy.

steps.title: Represent the hybrid path to GKE
steps.content: Represent the owner-approved hybrid route between the shared connectivity boundary and GKE without claiming a latency result.

connection.label: Hybrid path to Google Cloud
connection.description: Intended on-prem-to-GKE path; verify route, firewall, DNS, and reachability before treating it as operational.

steps.title: Represent the hybrid path to AWS
steps.content: Represent the owner-approved hybrid route between the shared connectivity boundary and AWS without choosing a network product or claiming a latency result.

connection.label: Hybrid path to AWS
connection.description: Intended on-prem-to-AWS path; verify route, firewall, DNS, and reachability before treating it as operational.

steps.title: Represent the hybrid path to Azure
steps.content: Represent the owner-approved hybrid route between the shared connectivity boundary and Azure without choosing a network product or claiming a latency result.

connection.label: Hybrid path to Azure
connection.description: Intended on-prem-to-Azure path; verify route, firewall, DNS, and reachability before treating it as operational.

steps.title: Define evidence for the under-100ms target
steps.content: The brief states network latency under 100ms but does not define covered paths, geography, load, measurement boundary, or statistic. Agree those details and measure the actual paths before claiming the target is met.

decision.question: How should the stated network-latency constraint be evaluated?
decision.chosen: Measure the agreed workload and control-plane paths against the under-100ms target after owners define path scope and measurement conditions.
decision.chosenReason: A topology diagram and an unspecified measurement boundary cannot establish that the stated latency target is achieved.

alternatives.option: Treat the target as already satisfied by choosing a cloud or network product
alternatives.tradeoff: Product choice alone does not prove end-to-end path latency.
Other required cloud and on-prem paths may behave differently and remain unverified.

properties.notes: Measure actual required workload and control-plane paths against the stated under-100ms target; agree path scope and measurement conditions before claiming compliance.

steps.title: Record the zero-trust service boundary
steps.content: Make workload identity, authenticated service communication, and authorization explicit. Validate supported controls and coverage per environment; treat mTLS as a target to test, not proof of enforcement or regulatory compliance. The brief does not specify a compliance framework.

decision.question: What should the service-mesh boundary require?
decision.chosen: Require authenticated workload identity and explicitly authorized service communication; validate identity trust, mesh controls, and per-workload coverage in each environment.
decision.chosenReason: The brief requires zero-trust networking and service mesh, but does not specify identity providers, exceptions, or platform compatibility.

alternatives.option: Trust traffic because it originates inside a cluster or cloud network
alternatives.tradeoff: Network location alone does not establish workload identity or authorization.

alternatives.option: Assume identical mesh capabilities across all environments
alternatives.tradeoff: Unsupported features or coverage gaps could leave paths without the intended controls.

steps.title: Add the observability boundary
steps.content: Use the existing Monitoring catalog node for the Cloud Monitoring role named in the hints. Capture resource health, fleet status, configuration drift, policy findings, and mesh and network observations without inventing thresholds.

component.label: Cloud Monitoring and Fleet Health
component.description: Operational view for cluster, policy, configuration, mesh, and path health.

properties.purpose: Collect and present available resource health, fleet registration, configuration reconciliation, policy findings, service-mesh signals, and measured network-path latency; define alert thresholds with service owners.

component.highlightReason: Cloud Monitoring is named in the hints and the existing catalog has a Monitoring component type.

steps.title: Monitor fleet registration and control health
steps.content: Expose registration status, control-plane reachability, and fleet-operation errors to the operator's monitoring view.

connection.label: Fleet health and registration
connection.description: Fleet state and management errors feed operational monitoring.

steps.title: Observe GKE resources
steps.content: Route available GKE resource and workload observations into the shared monitoring view; select metrics and thresholds with service owners.

connection.label: GKE resource observations
connection.description: GKE health and workload signals are available to the multi-cloud operations view.

steps.title: Observe AWS resources
steps.content: Route available AWS Kubernetes resource and workload observations into the shared monitoring view; confirm integration and ownership with the platform team.

connection.label: AWS resource observations
connection.description: AWS cluster health and workload signals are available to the multi-cloud operations view.

steps.title: Observe Azure resources
steps.content: Route available Azure Kubernetes resource and workload observations into the shared monitoring view; confirm integration and ownership with the platform team.

connection.label: Azure resource observations
connection.description: Azure cluster health and workload signals are available to the multi-cloud operations view.

steps.title: Observe on-prem resources
steps.content: Route available on-prem Kubernetes resource and workload observations into the shared monitoring view, including visibility into any collection gaps.

connection.label: On-prem resource observations
connection.description: On-prem cluster health and workload signals are available to the multi-cloud operations view.

steps.title: Review evidence before claiming readiness
steps.content: Check that each required environment has a verified fleet-registration path; desired state and policy findings have separate status; service-mesh identity controls cover the selected workloads; on-prem connectivity and monitoring gaps are visible; and the stated under-100ms target has been measured on owner-defined paths. The diagram records responsibilities and candidate flows; it does not prove provider support, policy compliance, security, or latency.
